idea-plugin.name: RepoLeap
idea-plugin.description:
Leap to any local Git repository in a few keystrokes: one shortcut, fuzzy search across all your repos, done. Stop digging through folders like it’s 1999.

Option+Command+I (macOS) or Alt+Shift+P (Windows/Linux) opens a search popup with every Git repository in the folders you configured. Type a few letters of the name or path, press Enter – and you are in the project.

Main features

  • One popup for all your repositories – any number of root folders, searched recursively (worktrees included) with a configurable depth and ignored folder names
  • Free-text search – several words in any order, matched against names and paths, fuzzy on names, with highlighted matches
  • Always the right order – pinned repositories first, then the one in the current window, then those open in other windows, then the rest; the best matches and recently opened repositories lead within each group
  • Jump instead of reopening – open repositories are marked (current window, other window) and choosing one brings exactly that window to the front
  • macOS window tabs – bring a repository that is open in another window into the current window as a tab (Shift+Enter)
  • Open the way you like – new window, current window or the IDE setting; Shift+Enter uses the alternative

More features

Press Tab (or right-click) on a repository for its actions:

  • Info – branch, upstream with ahead/behind, last commit, remotes, uncommitted and untracked files, commits that are not pushed anywhere, stashes
  • Open the remote in the browser – GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, Bitbucket Cloud, Bitbucket Server / Data Center, Azure DevOps, AWS CodeCommit, SourceHut, or your own rules
  • Close the project, show the folder in the system file manager, copy the path
  • Pin favorites to the top, hide repositories you never need
  • Rename the folder or move it to the Trash – with a warning about everything that would otherwise be lost (uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, stashes, no remote)

Scanning runs in the background, so the popup opens instantly.

Getting started

  1. Open Settings | Tools | RepoLeap and add the folders that contain your repositories.
  2. Press the shortcut, or use File | Open Repository….

The shortcut can be changed in Settings | Keymap (search for “Open Repository”).

Privacy

RepoLeap does not collect or transmit any data. Only if the type of a self-hosted git server can not be told from the remote URL, it asks that git server once whether it is a Bitbucket Server (can be switched off in the settings).

Feedback

Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub.
